# viettelcloud_security_group_rule (Resource)

Manage a Viettel Cloud security group rule.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The security group that owns the rules. Reference viettelcloud_security_group.id
# once that resource manages the group.
variable "security_group_id" {
  type        = string
  description = "Security group ID (UUID) to attach the rules to."
}

# Allow inbound SSH from anywhere.
resource "viettelcloud_security_group_rule" "ingress_ssh" {
  security_group   = { id = var.security_group_id }
  direction        = "ingress"
  protocol         = "tcp"
  port_range_min   = 22
  port_range_max   = 22
  remote_ip_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"
  description      = "Allow inbound SSH"
}

# Allow outbound HTTPS to anywhere.
resource "viettelcloud_security_group_rule" "egress_https" {
  security_group   = { id = var.security_group_id }
  direction        = "egress"
  protocol         = "tcp"
  port_range_min   = 443
  port_range_max   = 443
  remote_ip_prefix = "0.0.0.0/0"
  description      = "Allow outbound HTTPS"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `direction` (String) Direction of the rule: ingress or egress.
- `protocol` (String) Protocol filter. Supported values: ah, any, dccp, egp, esp, gre, hopopt, icmp, igmp, ip, ipip, ipv6-encap, ipv6-frag, ipv6-icmp, ipv6-nonxt, ipv6-opts, ipv6-route, ospf, pgm, rsvp, sctp, tcp, udp, udplite, vrrp.
- `security_group` (Attributes) Security group owning the rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--security_group))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description of the rule, the only attribute that can change in place. Omitting it preserves the backend value; set it to an empty string to clear it.
- `port_range_max` (Number) Upper bound of the allowed port range. It cannot be configured for ICMP protocols. Omitting it keeps whatever the backend assigned.
- `port_range_min` (Number) Lower bound of the allowed port range. It cannot be configured for ICMP protocols. Omitting it keeps whatever the backend assigned.
- `remote_ip_prefix` (String) CIDR allowed to reach the rule. Omitting it keeps whatever the backend assigned.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) Timestamp when the rule was created (RFC3339).
- `ethertype` (String) Address family assigned by the backend: ipv4 or ipv6.
- `id` (String) Security group rule ID (UUID).
- `region` (String) Region name inherited from the security group.
- `security_group_name` (String) Name of the security group owning the rule.
- `updated_at` (String) Timestamp when the rule was last updated (RFC3339).
